ruling: MIN-007 T2 (minutes:a296b0542ddd66fcd0679d34): O3 row mirror as a matrix instrument — full event rows + hash columns + append-only triggers + validateEventChain re-verification + chain-version keying; explicitly NOT backed up

reachabilityInvestigation.question: can AOS enumerate every raw chain event through a governed read path under the 1 MiB canonical limit?

findings.verdict: carries complete event records (id/streamId/sequence/occurredAt/priorHash/payload/payloadHash/eventHash) but canonicalJson refuses any workspace whose canonical export exceeds 1 MiB
findings.redProbe: export against the live TCRN-AOS partition on 2026-07-28 exited 1 with {"ok":false,"reasonCode":"INPUT_OVERSIZED","error":"Canonical input exceeds one MiB"} — the O3 target chain itself is already past the limit

findings.verdict: not an event read surface: these verbs plan, dry-run and validate canonical-exchange bundles whose chunk contents the CALLER supplies (contentBase64 in the request); none of them enumerates chain events, so they cannot carry events out of a workspace the caller cannot already read

findings.path: paginated read verbs (work-list, work-show, gate-list, conference-*-list)
findings.verdict: no event verb exists in the v0.7.0 roster; the ingest fallback for oversized chains returns an empty event family and reports it as not-read
technically sufficient, deliberately not taken: CONF-001 rules the data plane MCP/CLI-only, so this stays reported as a tension rather than silently implemented

reachabilityInvestigation.conclusion: a governed enumeration path exists (export) and the mirror is implemented against it; the path does not reach the live TCRN-AOS chain because that chain's canonical form already exceeds 1 MiB, so mirroring the switchover target waits on a W-side read verb
reachabilityInvestigation.wSideRequirementDraft: W 需要一个受治的分页事件读动词(例如 event-list --workspace --limit --offset,返回完整 EventRecord 含 priorHash/payloadHash/eventHash),使超过 1 MiB 的链也能在受治读面下被逐事件枚举;在它落地前,O3 行镜像对超限分区只能停在已实现未接线状态。

shape.table: aos_event_mirror (own disposable database file, never the domain one)
columns: chain_version (version keying: the ingest that appended the row)
shape.verifier: engine protocol validateEventChain + canonicalJson, imported read-only from the governed copy's built output; this repository implements no second canonicalization or hash rule
shape.ingestContract: full chain in, engine-validated whole; overlap with held rows compared by event hash and canonical bytes; divergence and shrinkage are named refusals, never overwrites; only rows past the held head are appended

notBackedUp.enforcedBy: own database file outside every backup manifest; both backup scripts' notClaimed lists now name the exclusion and why (a second restorable copy of chain history would be a divergence nobody could adjudicate)

cover: engine-built chain mirrors row-for-row with hash columns and engine-canonical bytes
later-version re-ingest appends and never rewrites held rows; idempotent at same head
divergent overlap refused (EVENT_MIRROR_DIVERGENCE); shrunken chain refused (EVENT_MIRROR_CHAIN_SHRANK); mirror untouched
tampered payload rejected by the engine validator before any write
UPDATE and DELETE rejected by triggers against real rows (matrix R1 A-side touchstone), rows unchanged
out-of-band tampering with stored canonical bytes turns self-verification red without relying on the triggers

redEvidence.mutation: append-only triggers removed from the mirror schema
redEvidence.result: 2 failing tests (append-only rejection, canonical-bytes tamper detection), 4 passing
INPUT_OVERSIZED — recorded above as the reachability red proof

notClaimed: the live TCRN-AOS partition is NOT mirrored: its canonical export exceeds 1 MiB and no governed event enumeration verb reaches it; wiring waits on the W-side requirement above
the mirror is evidence about what the governed read surface returned, not an independent witness of the chain's bytes on disk
chains small enough for export can be mirrored today; the test chain is engine-built (createEvent) rather than a live partition
